_provenance: Shipped defaults for bin/harness-stats.js. `line.keys` = the numbers that earn the one-line `[instr]` form. Owner ruling 2026-09-10: the pick was delegated ("you decide") — these are Claude's choice, not the owner's, and a project overrides them in <root>/.claude/harness-stats.json (line.keys replaces the list wholesale; sources merge by id). REVISED 2026-09-11 after the quality audit and the owner's ruling that cost is NOT the goal ("i don't care for cost in tokens or context. I CARE ABOUT Quality"): the previous pick led with the per-prompt injection tax and with `hints.strict_pct`, and both were wrong to headline. The tax is not what the owner optimises, and `hints.strict_pct` / `acted_on.*` are FALSE NEGATIVES — they ask whether a file was OPENED of a mechanism that injects the file's BODY, so they read 0 in every project while content scoring put real uptake at 68% (65/96 notes; athena-onboarding 41/55, athena-clientele 24/41). A headline key that reads 0 for a working mechanism is worse than no key: it argues for deleting what works. Why these five now: uptake.used_pct (did the surfaced material reach the answer — the whole point of the recall half), uptake.empty_fires (how often recall ran and declined, the other half of the same question), lens.refuted (the mechanism that actually catches defects, counted), turn_end.blocks_per_prompt (friction the owner feels), judge.ms.p95 (the one wait the owner feels). Kept out deliberately: every byte count.
